pilotSummary: Both repos implemented and unit-tested locally. Staging migration dry-run found and fixed a real performance defect before it ever reached a commit (see migrationPerfFinding below). Not yet committed/PR'd -- doing that next, gated on the staging migration's second (optimized) run finishing.

legacy_design_tools_changes.searchSitusByStreetKeys_rewrite: Dropped the SQL-side storedSitusLocalitySql predicate (kept only for the ILIKE prefix fallback, which still needs it to bound over-matching). Locality now applies in JS, AFTER checking uniqueness: a UNIQUE street-key hit resolves unless the candidate's OWN recorded locality (situs_city column, falling back to parsing situs_address ONLY when situs_address is actually comma-composed) field-by-field CONTRADICTS the query (both sides have a value for the same field and they differ). An unknown field on the candidate is never treated as a contradiction. Ambiguous (2+) candidates still narrow by the existing placeSearchLocalityMatches semantics, or come back as a named list when no locality is supplied at all.
legacy_design_tools_changes.realBugFoundAndFixedDuringImplementation: First cut of the uniqueness bypass used placeSearchLocalityMatches directly, which regressed an existing pre-registered safety test (908 Pine exists as both a genuine Bastrop AND a genuine Georgetown parcel; a query for Bastrop must never silently resolve to Georgetown just because a particular search only returned the Georgetown row). Root cause: placeSearchLocalityMatches fails closed on a merely-UNKNOWN stored field, which is correct for its original disambiguation job but wrong for 'is this a real contradiction' -- caught by re-running the FULL existing test suite, not just my new tests. Fixed with a field-by-field contradiction check (both sides present and different) instead of reusing that function for this purpose. All 58 pre-existing + 7 new tests pass after the fix.
legacy_design_tools_changes.secondBugFoundAndFixed: localityFromStoredRow initially fell back to localityFromStoredAddress(situsAddress) unconditionally when situs_city was blank. That function assumes the STORE's historical comma-composed shape ('908 PINE ST, BASTROP, TX'); a CAD-backfilled Travis row's situs_address is a BARE, comma-less street ('414 SPILLER LN'). Feeding a comma-less string to a function built to parse a locality TAIL misparsed street tokens into a bogus city, which then read as a false contradiction against the query's real city -- caught by my own new test ('city-qualified query resolves the SAME row even though situs_city is null') failing on first run. Fixed by only calling localityFromStoredAddress when situsAddress actually contains a comma.
legacy_design_tools_changes.budgetTiering: New BARE_SITUS_SEARCH_BUDGET_MS = 4_000, applied only when parsePlaceSearchLocality(query) finds no city/state/zip at all. Locality-qualified queries and any explicit budgetMs override keep SITUS_SEARCH_BUDGET_MS = 20_000 (MCP's 30s abort is unaffected). Root-caused live: the PE proxy (hauska-map api/pe-situs-search.ts) aborts its own fetch at UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000 -- four times shorter than this route's internal budget -- so a bare query needing the full ladder raced past the caller's patience and came back as an unlabelled 502, before this route's own honest SITUS_SEARCH_BUDGET_ERROR ever had a chance to fire.

hauska_map_changes.sourceLabelling: LookupResult.source narrowed from the generic LookupKind ('parcel-node-id'|'address') to LookupResolvedSource ('parcel-node-id'|'situs'|'geocoded'). 'situs' covers every resolution the situs index itself produced, INCLUDING an address-point rooftop hit or a caller-trusted rooftop fed into fetchBuildableEnvelope as an explicit point (the resolver's own documented preference order honors an explicit point verbatim, no geocode -- confirmed by reading txgioAddressResolve.ts's RESOLUTION PREFERENCE comment). 'geocoded' is set ONLY for the bare address-only ladder (no situs hit, no trusted point at all), which is the one case that actually reaches Nominatim. This nuance mattered: an earlier, simpler 'anything through fetchBuildableEnvelope is geocoded' rule mislabelled the address-point-rooftop test case, caught by re-running the existing test suite.
hauska_map_changes.uiAdvisory: New SearchBar `advisory` prop (rendered in the same slot pattern as the existing `error` prop, lighter tone) plus ExplorerMap `lookupAdvisory` state, set to a labelled notice ('Matched by approximate address search -- no property record found for this address.') only when found.source === 'geocoded'. This is the visible 'UI saying so on the card' the mission asks for at the Find-box submit level.
hauska_map_changes.notImplementedThisPass_deferred: Typeahead DROPDOWN suggestion-level labelling/sort (distinguishing a geocoded Photon suggestion from a situs suggestion inline in the list before submit) -- mergeSearchSuggestions already documents and appears to implement 'situs ahead of geocoder' ordering, so the gap here is only the visual distinguishing mark on individual dropdown rows, not ordering. Also deferred: parcel-lookup.ts step 5 (bare house+street query, e.g. '908 Pine' with no suffix, running the situs search before refusing as ambiguous) -- none of the five P-172 probe-set queries are bare-house-street shaped, so this is a mission stretch goal beyond what the probe predicate measures, and I did not want to spend remaining budget on an unmeasured behavior change with no test coverage of my own building it. Both are named in leave_behind.

migrationPerfFinding.what: First cut of migration 0100 reused the full ~30-call regexp_replace normalization expression (migration 0058's index expression) to test cad_property.situs_address for blankness too. cad_property has NO functional index matching that expression (only txgio_parcel/txgio_address do, per migration 0058) -- confirmed via `pg_indexes` catalog read: cad_property's only index is the (county_fips, prop_id, tax_year) primary key. The predicate therefore forced a per-row evaluation of the full regex chain across every Travis cad_property row (7.6M rows / 3.6 GB total table, 2026-09-12 pg_class catalog read). Ran past 25 minutes on the staging branch before I aborted it.
migrationPerfFinding.fix: Rewrote the cad_property-side predicate to a cheap, non-regex blank check (`situs_address IS NOT NULL AND btrim(situs_address) <> '' AND btrim(situs_address) NOT LIKE ',%'`), which answers the same semantic question ('does this CAD row have real street text') without the regex chain. The txgio_parcel side of the migration KEEPS the full normalized expression unchanged, because that table has the supporting index and correctness there must stay byte-identical to what the search route itself treats as blank.
